identity.title: Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-time Consistency Models

problem.claim: Develop continuous-time consistency models (CMs) that support fast sampling without the instability limiting existing formulations.

gap.claim: Discretized-timestep CMs add hyperparameters and may incur discretization errors, while continuous-time approaches have had limited success because of training instability.

contributions.claim: A simplified framework unifying prior diffusion-model and CM parameterizations and identifying reported root causes of instability.
Improvements to diffusion-process parameterization, network architecture, and training objectives based on the framework.
A continuous-time CM training approach scaled to 1.5B parameters on ImageNet 512×512 and using two sampling steps.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by combining a simplifying unified theoretical framework with targeted changes that enable continuous-time CM training at the reported scale.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report training a continuous-time CM with 1.5B parameters on ImageNet 512×512.
Using two sampling steps, the authors report FID scores of 2.06 on CIFAR-10, 1.48 on ImageNet 64×64, and 1.88 on ImageNet 512×512.
The authors report narrowing the FID gap with the best existing diffusion models to within 10%.

narrative_sequence.summary: CMs target fast diffusion-model sampling, but discretized training introduces hyperparameters and possible discretization errors; continuous-time training is limited by instability.
The paper presents a simplified framework unifying diffusion-model and CM parameterizations and attributes instability to specific root causes.
It derives changes to process parameterization, architecture, and training objectives.
The resulting approach is reported to scale to 1.5B parameters and achieve the listed two-step FID results, within 10% of leading diffusion-model FIDs.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a theoretical unification and instability analysis directly to changes in parameterization, architecture, and objectives, then to scale and benchmark outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its method-to-evidence chain easier to assess by connecting diagnosis, intervention, and measured consequences.
lessons.application: For a new generative-model method, explicitly map each diagnosed failure mode to a design change and report benchmarks under the same stated operating constraint.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when the work is primarily exploratory or lacks a concrete mechanistic diagnosis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baselines, evaluation protocols, statistical variability, or whether all reported FIDs use identical sampling and training conditions.
The claimed root causes, scale distinction, and comparison gap are author-reported and cannot be independently assessed from the abstract alone.
